answer: Proof of Burn mechanisms mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to destroy native tokens to harbor voting weight. Like an ember consuming fuel, the economic cost of identity creation increases linearly, creating a dune of cumulative capital expenditure that makes mass-pseudonymity prohibitively expensive. An attacker must forfeit liquid assets to achieve influence, ensuring that Sybil clusters are economically irrational compared to the network security benefits provided.
